question.text: A farmer growing cotton (kharif crop) wants to protect against falling prices during the harvest season (September-January). Which strategy would be most appropriate?

answer.text: Sell cotton futures contracts before the harvest season begins
Buy cotton futures contracts during the harvest season
Wait and sell in the spot market at harvest time

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, a producer who fears falling prices should sell futures to lock in the selling price for the upcoming harvest, hedging the seasonal price decline. The Trap: Buying futures gives long exposure (wrong direction for a producer). Selling in the spot market at harvest accepts the lower seasonal price. Buying calls profits from price rises, not declines. Note: The workbook supports selling futures during sowing or before the upcoming harvest to lock the selling price; it does not prescribe a specific "2-3 months ahead" timing rule.
